name: Visceral Heterotaxy Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No standardized formal criteria; diagnosis based on clinical and imaging findings

criteria.description: Presence of abnormal arrangement of thoracic and/or abdominal organs inconsistent with normal situs solitus or situs inversus
Complex congenital heart defects including atrioventricular septal defects, transposition of great arteries, or anomalous pulmonary venous return
Asplenia or polysplenia detected by imaging or surgical exploration

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of abnormal organ arrangement plus at least one major congenital cardiac malformation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing and family history may support diagnosis but are not definitive.

pathognomonic.notes: Includes situs ambiguous with neither normal nor mirror-image organ placement
searchTerms: abnormal positioning of chest and abdominal organs

pathognomonic.notes: Often includes atrioventricular septal defects and anomalous pulmonary venous return
Leads to increased risk of infections
searchTerms: spleen abnormalities including no spleen or many spleens

common.symptomName: Respiratory infections due to impaired mucociliary clearance
common.notes: Secondary to ciliary dysfunction in some cases
searchTerms: lung infections from poor mucus clearance
respiratory infections due to cilia dysfunction
frequent chest infections from impaired airway cleaning

common.symptomName: Congestive heart failure symptoms in infancy

occasional.notes: Reported in some patients with heterotaxy
Such as horseshoe kidney or renal agenesis

searchTerms: irregular heartbeats linked to organ arrangement
heart rhythm problems from organ positioning

rare.symptomName: Neurological abnormalities due to ischemic events
rare.notes: Secondary to embolic events from cardiac defects
searchTerms: brain or nerve problems from lack of blood flow

rare.notes: Rarely reported hypothyroidism or adrenal insufficiency

laboratory: Blood smear showing Howell-Jolly bodies indicating functional asplenia
imaging: Chest and abdominal X-ray or ultrasound showing abnormal organ situs
Echocardiography revealing complex congenital heart defects
Abdominal CT or MRI demonstrating splenic anomalies and intestinal malrotation
genetic: Mutations in genes related to left-right axis patterning such as ZIC3, CFC1, and NODAL in some cases
other: Functional asplenia leading to increased susceptibility to encapsulated bacterial infections

distinguishingFeatures: Complete mirror-image reversal of organ placement without complex cardiac defects
Recurrent respiratory infections with normal organ situs or situs inversus
Absence of complex congenital heart defects

redFlags: Severe cyanosis or heart failure in neonate
Signs of sepsis in asplenic patients
references: Lin AE, et al. Heterotaxy: associated conditions and hospital-based prevalence in newborns. Genet Med. 2014.
Mahadevan V, et al. Clinical and genetic aspects of heterotaxy syndrome. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2017.
Brueckner M. Genetics of heterotaxy syndromes. Curr Opin Cardiol. 2012.
